# Code of Conduct

## Our standard

This is a project for people who run and extend document systems for their organisations. We want it to be a place where questions are welcome and problems get solved. In every project space (issues, pull requests, discussions) we expect people to:

- be respectful and patient, especially with newcomers and with people working in a second language;
- give specific, constructive feedback and accept it graciously;
- assume good intent, and ask when something is unclear;
- keep discussions about the work.

Not acceptable: harassment, insults, discrimination, personal attacks, publishing other people's private information (including their credentials or confidential customer data), and sustained disruption.

## Scope and enforcement

This applies to all project spaces and to anyone representing the project in public. Maintainers may edit or remove comments, issues and contributions that do not follow this code, and may ban people who repeatedly or seriously violate it.

To report a problem, use GitHub's private reporting (Security → Report a vulnerability, choosing "conduct concern" in the title) or contact the maintainer through the profile of the repository owner. Reports are handled privately and in good faith.

This Code of Conduct is adapted from the principles of the [Contributor Covenant](https://www.contributor-covenant.org), version 2.1.
